s0.open.text: This is Root. [[0.35]] It looks like a board game about woodland animals, and it is a war game.

s0.asym.text: It has one strange property. No two players are playing by the same rules. The cat scores by building. The birds score by nesting. The mouse alliance scores by making the forest sympathetic to her cause.

s0.pieces.text: Different pieces, [[0.3]] different actions, [[0.3]] different ways to win. Six factions, [[0.3]] six separate rulebooks.

s0.question.text: So what makes it one game?

s1.obvious.text: The obvious answer is the scoreboard. Everybody scores differently, but everybody scores onto the same track, and the first player to reach thirty points immediately wins.

s1.corners.text: One finish line. [[0.4]] Except a shared finish line is not a shared game. Suppose the cat builds in her corner and the birds nest in theirs, and neither ever has to look at the other. Both scores climb. Nothing has made them meet.

s1.need.text: That is a race, not a war. Something has to force them into the same room.

s2.map.text: Here is the Woodland. Clearings, joined by paths. A clearing is adjacent to every clearing a path links it to, and almost everything in this game travels along those paths.

s2.suit.text: Every clearing has a suit. [[0.3]] Fox, rabbit, or mouse. The cards share those three, plus birds — and a bird card is wild, so it can be treated as any suit you like.

s2.slots.text: Every clearing has slots, shown as white boxes, and a building fills one. Four start the game filled with ruins.

s2.sentence.text: And now the sentence the whole game hangs on. [[0.5]] The ruler of a clearing is the player with the most total warriors and buildings in it.

s2.notcount.text: Tokens do not count. Pawns do not count. And if two players are tied, nobody rules it at all.

s2.cant.text: From up here you cannot see any of that. [[0.35]] You have to count. [[0.5]] So stop looking at it like a map.

s2.tilt.text: Warriors and buildings are the things that count, so let them be the things that have height.

s2.skyline.text: Rule is a skyline. [[0.4]] Tallest tower in the clearing holds it. Level towers, and nobody does.

s3.prize.text: Ruling a clearing is not a prize. [[0.35]] It is a permission slip.

s3.move.text: To move, you take any number of your warriors from one clearing to one adjacent clearing. And you must rule the origin, or the destination, or both.

s3.tie.text: Level the two towers, and the move becomes illegal. You cannot leave a clearing you do not overtop, unless you already overtop where you are going.

s3.build.text: To build, you need a clearing you rule [[0.3]] and a slot that is open.

s3.craft.text: Even crafting is paid in clearings. A card's cost is paid by activating your own pieces, and a piece's suit is the suit of its clearing.

s3.bolted.text: So whatever private machine your faction runs on, it is bolted to this board. There is no corner to be left alone in.

s4.phases.text: A turn is three phases, always in this order. Birdsong, before the day. Daylight, where most of the acting happens. Evening, where you draw and some factions score.

s4.quiet.text: Most of Daylight is quiet. Draw, craft, move, build. [[0.4]] Battle is the loud one.

s4.choose.text: You choose a clearing where you have warriors, choose somebody else standing there to defend, and roll both dice.

s4.rolls.text: The attacker deals hits equal to the higher roll. The defender deals hits equal to the lower one.

s4.cap.text: But you can never deal more hits from the dice than you have warriors in that clearing. The roll is only a ceiling. [[0.35]] Your tower is the real limit.

s4.defenceless.text: And if the defender has no warriors there at all, the attacker deals one extra hit.

s4.simul.text: Then both sides deal their hits at the same time. Warriors come off first. Buildings and tokens only once every warrior is gone.

s4.vp.text: Every enemy building or token you remove is worth a victory point. [[0.4]] And the skyline changes hands.

s5.turn.text: Now the part that looks like chaos. Six factions, six rulebooks. [[0.35]] And every one of them is written against that same sentence.

s5.cat.text: The Marquise de Cat plays it straight, and hardest. She scores by building, and a building is height, so her score and her grip on the map are the same object.

s5.cat2.text: Building costs wood, and the wood comes from sawmills she already built. Her engine feeds itself, as long as she holds the ground under it.

s5.eyrie.text: The Eyrie Dynasties edit the sentence. They rule a clearing when they are merely tied for most. [[0.35]] Never an empty one, but a tie is enough.

s5.eyrie2.text: They score every Evening for roosts standing on the map, so they grow faster than anyone. And they are bound by the Decree. Cards go onto it every Birdsong, and every action on it must be taken. Miss one, and they fall into turmoil.

s5.alliance.text: The Woodland Alliance ignores the sentence. She scores by placing sympathy, and sympathy is a token, [[0.3]] and tokens do not count toward rule. Her score is invisible to the skyline.

s5.outrage.text: It is worse than that. Move warriors into a clearing she has made sympathetic, and Outrage makes you hand her a card. Attacking her funds her.

s5.vagabond.text: The Vagabond deletes the sentence. He is a pawn, not a warrior. He cannot rule a clearing, he cannot stop anyone else ruling one, and he cannot be removed from the map. He walks where he likes, and scores by carrying items and making friends with people busy killing each other.

s5.cult.text: The Lizard Cult overwrites the sentence. Wherever the Cult has a garden, the Cult rules. Height does not enter into it.

s5.riverfolk.text: And the Riverfolk Company goes around it. A river runs through the Woodland, and it is a path for them and for nobody else. They swim along it no matter who rules either end, and then they sell passage to the other five.

s6.setup.text: Setup. The Marquise takes a corner, puts her keep in it, and garrisons one warrior in every clearing except the corner diagonally opposite.

s6.setup2.text: Which is where the Eyrie start. [[0.4]] The Alliance starts with nothing on the board at all.

s6.t1.text: Turn one, the Marquise. Birdsong, a wood token appears at each sawmill. Daylight, three actions.

s6.t1build.text: She builds. The wood is spent, the slot fills, and she scores the points the space underneath reveals.

s6.t1march.text: Then she marches, which is two moves, and her towers get taller where she wants them. Evening, she draws.

s6.t2.text: Turn two, the Eyrie. Birdsong, a card goes onto the Decree. Daylight, they must resolve every column of it, left to right.

s6.t2battle.text: Move: five birds cross into the clearing the cat has just built in. [[0.3]] Battle: the rabbit card lets them fight there.

s6.t2dice.text: Higher roll to the attacker, lower to the defender, both capped by the warriors actually standing there, both dealt at the same moment.

s6.t2flip.text: The cat's tower falls to two, and the clearing is the Eyrie's. They build a roost on it. Evening, the birds score for every roost on the map.

s6.t3.text: Turn three, the Alliance. Birdsong, she spreads sympathy, spending supporters that match the clearing, plus one more because three or more enemy warriors are standing in it.

s6.t3score.text: She scores. [[0.4]] And she has still not placed a single warrior on the board.

s6.reply.text: Now watch what the obvious reply costs the cat.

s6.outrage.text: She marches in to stamp it out. [[0.35]] Outrage. She hands the Alliance a card matching that clearing.

s6.revolt.text: Which the Alliance spends, next Birdsong, on a revolt. Every enemy piece in the clearing is removed, and a base goes up in their place.

s6.revolt2.text: A point for the sawmill. A point for the roost. [[0.4]] And the clearing belongs to the faction that never marched a single warrior into it.

s7.restate.text: So. [[0.4]] No two players in Root are playing by the same rules. What makes it one game?

s7.answer.text: They are not playing different games. They are playing different answers to the same question. [[0.5]] Who holds this clearing?

s7.each.text: The cat answers with buildings. The birds answer by tying. The alliance answers by not needing to hold it. The vagabond answers that he never can.

s7.close.text: Six rulebooks. One sentence. One map. [[0.5]] The rules differ. The ground does not.
